Modified assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- Core policy tone remains hawkish: inflation has “eased somewhat but remains elevated,” the funds rate was raised to 4.5–4.75%, “ongoing increases” are anticipated, and balance-sheet reduction continues.
- SLOOS lens points to a tighter credit channel and softer demand: banks tightened standards on C&I and CRE loans; banks reported weaker demand for nonfarm nonresidential, construction/land development, and multifamily; firms cited decreased financing needs for plant/equipment, M&A, inventories, and accounts receivable; foreign banks also reported weaker C&I demand. These factors suggest restrictive policy is being reinforced by tighter credit supply and waning loan demand, increasing downside growth risks.
- Net effect: more negative than the prior -0.13 given evident tightening and weaker demand in SLOOS, though tempered by ongoing labor-market resilience and bank capitalization.
